title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON RESTORATION OF HONOR OF VICTIMS OF THE OCTOBER 27 BUDDHIST PERSECUTION AND RELATED MATTERS
title_original: 10ㆍ27법난 피해자의 명예회복 등에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on Restoration of Honor of Victims of the October 27 Buddhist Persecution and Related Matters and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Composition and Operation of Deliberation Committee for Restoration of Honor of Victims of October 27 Buddhist Persecution)
(1) The Deliberation Committee for Restoration of Honor of Victims of the October 27 Buddhist Persecution under Article 3 of the Act on Restoration of Honor of Victims of the October 27 Buddhist Persecution and Related Matters (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee") shall consist of the members under subparagraphs 1 through 3 appointed by the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism and up to seven members under subparagraph 4 commissioned by the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism with consideration given to gender: <Amended on Nov. 11, 2011; Mar. 23, 2013; Jan. 6, 2015; June 8, 2016; Apr. 11, 2023>
1. The head of the Religious Affairs Office of the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism;
2. The Director General for Legal Affairs of the Ministry of National Defense;
3. The Director General for Veterans Culture Policy of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs;
4. Persons with extensive knowledge and experience in the relevant fields.
(2) The chairperson of the Committee shall convene and preside over its meetings.
(3) Where the chairperson is unable to perform his or her duties due to unavoidable circumstances, a member designated in advance by the chairperson shall act on his or her behalf.
(4) A majority of the incumbent members shall constitute a quorum for a meeting of the Committee, and resolutions shall be adopted by the affirmative votes of a majority of the members present.
(5) Where a member who is a public official is unable to attend a Committee meeting due to unavoidable circumstances, the public official holding the position immediately below that member may attend as a proxy and perform the member's duties. <Added on June 8, 2016>
(6) The term of office of a Committee member shall be two years, and the member may be reappointed consecutively only twice; provided, the term of office of a member who is a public official shall be the period during which the member holds the relevant position. <Added on June 8, 2016>

Article 2-2 (Dismissal of Commissioned Members) The Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism may dismiss a member under Article 2 (1) 4 from his or her commission where the member falls under any of the following:
1. Where the member becomes unable to perform his or her duties due to a mental or physical disability;
2. Where the member has committed misconduct related to his or her duties;
3. Where the member is deemed unsuitable as a member due to neglect of duty, impairment of dignity, or other grounds;
4. Where the member personally expresses that it is difficult to perform his or her duties.

Article 3 (Composition of Working Committee)
(1) A working committee may be established within the Committee to review in advance agenda items to be deliberated and resolved upon by the Committee and to handle matters delegated by the Committee.
(2) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the working committee shall be determined by the chairperson of the Committee following a resolution of the Committee.

Article 4 Deleted. <Aug. 20, 2013>

Article 5 (Allowances and Expenses)
(1) Allowances may be paid within budgetary limits to members attending the Committee or working committee; provided, this shall not apply where a member who is a public official attends in direct connection with duties under his or her jurisdiction.
(2) Travel expenses and actual expenses may be paid within budgetary limits to witnesses or persons giving statements who appear before the Committee, etc. pursuant to Article 7 of the Act.

Article 6 (Matters concerning Support Related to Restoration of Honor) The term "matters concerning support prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 3 (2) 5 of the Act means the following: <Amended on Aug. 20, 2013>
1. Matters concerning support for commemorative events for the restoration of honor;
2. Other matters necessary to implement matters for the restoration of honor resolved upon by the Committee.

Article 6-2 Deleted. <June 8, 2016>

Article 7 Deleted. <June 8, 2016>

Article 8 Deleted. <June 8, 2016>

Article 9 (Applications for Medical Support Payments)
(1) A person wishing to apply for a medical support payment under Article 5 of the Act shall submit an application for medical support payment in attached Form 4 to the application receiving institution designated by the Committee, together with the following documents: <Amended on June 8, 2016>
1. A statement of the circumstances of harm in attached Form 2;
2. One copy of a power of attorney for application for (receipt of) a medical support payment in attached Form 3 (limited to applications made by a proxy pursuant to paragraph (2)), and one copy of the victim's certificate of family relations (limited to cases where the proxy is a family member), one copy;
3. One copy of other supporting materials substantiating the grounds for the application.
(2) Where a person wishing to apply under paragraph (1) is unable to apply personally due to emigration, hospitalization, or other unavoidable circumstances, he or she may appoint a proxy by a power of attorney for application for (receipt of) a medical support payment in attached Form 3, confirmed by a person falling under any of the following: <Amended on June 8, 2016>
1. In the case of a stay abroad due to emigration, etc.: The head of an overseas diplomatic mission;
2. In the case of hospitalization: The head of the relevant medical institution;
3. In the case of confinement in a correctional institution, etc.: The head of the institution of confinement;
4. In other cases: The head of the Eup, Myeon, or Dong of the person's address.
(3) Where the documents specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) are not attached to an application for a medical support payment received under that paragraph, the application receiving institution shall require the applicant to supplement them, and shall verify a certified copy of the applicant's resident registration record through the joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act; provided, where the applicant does not consent to verification, the applicant shall be required to attach the relevant document. <Added on June 8, 2016>

Article 10 (Calculation of Medical Support Payments) Medical support payments, including treatment costs, care costs, and costs of purchasing assistive devices under Article 5 (1) of the Act, shall be amounts calculated in the following manner: <Amended on July 2, 2019; Sept. 29, 2021; Oct. 1, 2025>
1. Treatment costs shall be the amount determined by the Committee in consideration of equity with other victims, based on an estimate of treatment costs issued by a national general hospital, a hospital affiliated with a medical college (excluding branch hospitals), or a hospital designated by the Committee (hereinafter referred to as "designated hospitals, etc."); provided, where a designated hospital, etc. recognizes the need for treatment costs but is unable to estimate them, the amount shall be determined by the Committee with reference to treatment costs in similar cases.
2. Care costs shall be paid where, according to a medical certificate issued by a designated hospital, etc., the victim is recognized as having a physical disability even after full recovery that makes it difficult to engage in activities without another person's care. The amount shall be calculated by multiplying the amount determined by the Committee within the range of nursing allowances under Article 26 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State by the average remaining life expectancy published by the National Data Office as at June 29, 2008, the enforcement date of the Act.
3. Costs of purchasing assistive devices shall, where the need to wear an assistive device is recognized according to a medical certificate issued by a designated hospital, etc., be the market purchase price multiplied by the number of purchases deemed necessary, based on the usable life of the assistive device, during the average remaining life expectancy published by the National Data Office as at June 29, 2008, the enforcement date of the Act.

Article 11 (Decisions) Upon deciding to make a medical support payment in response to an application under Article 9, the Committee shall prepare a written decision on medical support payment in attached Form 6, and all members present at the Committee meeting shall sign it or affix their names and seals. <Amended on June 8, 2016>

Article 12 (Notification of Decisions)
(1) Where the Committee decides to make a medical support payment pursuant to Article 11, it shall retain the original written decision on medical support payment and serve on the applicant one copy of a notice of the decision on medical support payment in attached Form 9 or attached Form 10, accompanied by one authenticated copy of the written decision. In such cases, where the applicant is the victim's proxy, one certified copy of the written decision on medical support payment shall also be served on the victim. <Amended on June 8, 2016; Nov. 12, 2024>
1. Deleted. <June 8, 2016>
2. Deleted. <June 8, 2016>
(2) The original written decision on medical support payment under the former part of paragraph (1) may be retained as an electronic document or digitized document under Article 5 of the Framework Act on Electronic Documents and Transactions. <Added on Nov. 12, 2024>

Article 13 (Applications for Reconsideration) An applicant notified of a decision on medical support payment under Article 12 (1) who wishes to apply for reconsideration shall submit an application for reconsideration in attached Form 11 to the Committee within 30 days after the date on which the notice of the decision on medical support payment is served, together with materials proving the grounds for reconsideration. <Amended on Nov. 11, 2011; June 8, 2016; Nov. 12, 2024>
1. Deleted. <Nov. 11, 2011>
2. Deleted. <Nov. 11, 2011>

Article 14 (Consent and Claims) Where an applicant notified of a decision on medical support payment under Article 12 (1) wishes to receive the medical support payment, the applicant shall submit a consent and claim form in attached Form 13 to the Committee, together with the following documents: <Amended on June 8, 2016; Nov. 12, 2024>
1. One certificate of seal impression or certificate of personal signature (limited to cases where the consent and claim form is signed);
2. One copy of a financial institution account passbook.

Article 15 (Paying Institution) Medical support payments determined by the Committee shall be made by the Committee; provided, the practical payment procedures may be entrusted to the Bank of Korea, including its national treasury agencies.

Article 16 (Time of Payment) Medical support payments shall be made within 15 days after the date on which a claim for payment under Article 14 is made.

Article 17 (Fact-Finding Investigations)
(1) With respect to a person who has applied for a medical support payment under Article 9 and whose application details cannot be verified through the Committee's own investigation, the Committee may notify the Minister of National Defense, the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism, the Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency, etc. of those details and request verification of their truth pursuant to Article 7 (1) of the Act. <Amended on June 8, 2016>
(2) The Minister of National Defense, the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism, the Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency, etc., upon receiving a request for verification under paragraph (1), shall verify the truth of the application details within three months after receiving the request, prepare a certificate of facts concerning harm suffered in the October 27 Buddhist persecution in attached Form 14, and notify the Committee thereof together with supporting documents.

Article 18 (Processing of Sensitive Information and Personally Identifiable Information) Where unavoidable for performing affairs concerning medical support payments under Article 5 of the Act, the Committee may process materials containing health information under Article 23 of the Personal Information Protection Act or resident registration numbers under subparagraph 1 of Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act. <Amended on June 8, 2016>
1. Deleted. <June 8, 2016>
2. Deleted. <June 8, 2016>
